title: Lead RRP firm and renovator certification and training study guide
description: Lead RRP study guide on firm certification, certified renovator and dust sampling technician duties, refreshers and courses: 40 CFR 745.89-745.91 and 745.225.
intro: This guide sets out what the federal rule text in 40 CFR Part 745 says about certification and training under the lead Renovation, Repair and Painting (RRP) rule: firm certification, re-certification and amendment and the firm's responsibilities (745.89), renovator and dust sampling technician certification, refreshers, renovator duties and on-the-job worker training (745.90), suspension and revocation (745.91), the fee exemption and no-fee items (745.92, without fee amounts), and the renovator and dust sampling technician course and refresher requirements for accredited training programs (745.225 in Subpart L). The Certified Renovator credential is earned only by completing an accredited course; goraedu is not a training provider and this guide is not that course or its exam. EPA certification applies in States and Indian Tribal areas without an authorized renovation program. Your State or Tribe may run its own authorized program, so check its rules too. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

topics.name: Firm certification

points.text: Firms that perform renovations for compensation must apply to EPA electronically for certification to perform renovations or dust sampling.
points.quote: Firms that perform renovations for compensation must electronically apply to EPA for certification to perform renovations or dust sampling.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: To apply, a firm submits a completed "Application for Firms" signed by an authorized agent of the firm and pays electronically at least the correct amount of fees.
points.quote: To apply, a firm must submit to EPA a completed “Application for Firms,” signed by an authorized agent of the firm, and pay electronically at least the correct amount of fees.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: EPA takes one of the listed actions within 90 days of receiving the application. It approves the application if it is complete and the environmental compliance history of the firm, its principals, or its key employees does not show an unwillingness or inability to maintain compliance with environmental statutes or regulations.
points.quote: EPA will take one of the following actions within 90 days of the date the application is received: (i) EPA will approve a firm's application if EPA determines that it is complete and that the environmental compliance history of the firm, its principals, or its key employees does not show an unwillingness or inability to maintain compliance with environmental statutes or regulations.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: An approved firm receives a certificate with an expiration date not more than 5 years from the approval date. EPA firm certification covers renovations in any State or Indian Tribal area that does not have a renovation program authorized under subpart Q.
points.quote: When EPA approves a firm's application, EPA will issue the firm a certificate with an expiration date not more than 5 years from the date the application is approved. EPA certification allows the firm to perform renovations covered by this section in any State or Indian Tribal area that does not have a renovation program that is authorized under subpart Q of this part.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: EPA asks a firm to supplement its application if EPA determines the application is incomplete. The firm must then submit the requested information or pay the additional fees within 30 days of the date of the request.
points.quote: EPA will request a firm to supplement its application if EPA determines that the application is incomplete. If EPA requests a firm to supplement its application, the firm must submit the requested information or pay the additional fees within 30 days of the date of the request.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If EPA does not approve an initial application, it sends a letter giving the reason and does not refund the fees. The firm may reapply at any time with a new, complete application that includes the correct fees.
points.quote: EPA will send the firm a letter giving the reason for not approving the application. EPA will not refund the application fees. A firm may reapply for certification at any time by filing a new, complete application that includes the correct amount of fees.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.notCovered: The fee amounts in 745.92 are not stated on this site. EPA certification covers States and Indian Tribal areas that do not have a renovation program authorized under subpart Q; where a State or Tribe has one, check that program's rules.

points.text: To keep its certification, a firm must be re-certified by EPA every 5 years.
points.quote: To maintain its certification, a firm must be re-certified by EPA every 5 years.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A re-certification application is timely if it is submitted electronically 90 days or more before the current certification expires. If it is complete and timely, the current certification stays in effect until its expiration date or until EPA makes a final decision on the application, whichever is later.
points.quote: An application for re-certification is timely if it is electronically submitted 90 days or more before the date the firm's current certification expires. If the firm's application is complete and timely, the firm's current certification will remain in effect until its expiration date or until EPA has made a final decision to approve or disapprove the re-certification application, whichever is later.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If a complete application is submitted less than 90 days before expiration and EPA does not approve it before the expiration date, the certification expires and the firm cannot conduct renovations until EPA approves the re-certification.
points.quote: If the firm submits a complete re-certification application less than 90 days before its current certification expires, and EPA does not approve the application before the expiration date, the firm's current certification will expire and the firm will not be able to conduct renovations until EPA approves its re-certification application.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A firm that fails to obtain re-certification before its certification expires must not perform renovations or dust sampling until it is certified anew under paragraph (a) of 745.89.
points.quote: If the firm fails to obtain recertification before the firm's current certification expires, the firm must not perform renovations or dust sampling until it is certified anew pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: When EPA approves a re-certification, the new certificate expires 5 years from the date the firm's current certification expires.
points.quote: When EPA approves a firm's application for re-certification, EPA will issue the firm a new certificate with an expiration date 5 years from the date that the firm's current certification expires.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A firm must amend its certification within 90 days of a change to information in its most recent application. If it does not, it may not perform renovations or dust sampling until the certification is amended.
points.quote: A firm must amend its certification within 90 days of the date a change occurs to information included in the firm's most recent application. If the firm fails to amend its certification within 90 days of the date the change occurs, the firm may not perform renovations or dust sampling until its certification is amended.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Amending a certification does not change its expiration date.
points.quote: Amending a certification does not affect the certification expiration date.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Firm responsibilities

points.text: Firms performing renovations must ensure that everyone performing renovation activities on the firm's behalf is either a certified renovator or has been trained by a certified renovator in accordance with 745.90 (one of the options).
points.quote: Firms performing renovations must ensure that: (1) All individuals performing renovation activities on behalf of the firm are either certified renovators or have been trained by a certified renovator in accordance with § 745.90.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A firm performing renovations must also ensure that a certified renovator is assigned to each renovation the firm performs and carries out all of the certified renovator responsibilities in 745.90 (745.89(d)(2)).
points.quote: A certified renovator is assigned to each renovation performed by the firm and discharges all of the certified renovator responsibilities identified in § 745.90.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The firm must ensure that all renovations it performs follow the work practice standards in 745.85 (745.89(d)(3)).
points.quote: All renovations performed by the firm are performed in accordance with the work practice standards in § 745.85.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The firm must ensure that the pre-renovation education requirements of 745.84 have been performed (745.89(d)(4)).
points.quote: The pre-renovation education requirements of § 745.84 have been performed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The firm must ensure that the recordkeeping requirements of 745.86 are met (745.89(d)(5)).
points.quote: The recordkeeping requirements of § 745.86 are met.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.89, Firm certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.notCovered: The work practice standards (745.85), pre-renovation education (745.84) and recordkeeping (745.86) requirements themselves are not set out in this guide.

topics.name: Renovator and dust sampling technician certification

points.text: To become a certified renovator or certified dust sampling technician, an individual must successfully complete the appropriate course accredited by EPA under 745.225 or by an authorized State or Tribal program (one of the options). The course completion certificate is the proof of certification.
points.quote: To become a certified renovator or certified dust sampling technician, an individual must successfully complete the appropriate course accredited by EPA under § 745.225 or by a State or Tribal program that is authorized under subpart Q of this part. The course completion certificate serves as proof of certification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: EPA renovator certification covers renovations, and EPA dust sampling technician certification covers dust clearance sampling under 745.85(c), in any State or Indian Tribal area that does not have a renovation program authorized under subpart Q.
points.quote: EPA renovator certification allows the certified individual to perform renovations covered by this section in any State or Indian Tribal area that does not have a renovation program that is authorized under subpart Q of this part. EPA dust sampling technician certification allows the certified individual to perform dust clearance sampling under § 745.85(c) in any State or Indian Tribal area that does not have a renovation program that is authorized under subpart Q of this part.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: People who completed an accredited abatement worker or supervisor course, or an EPA, HUD, or EPA/HUD model renovation training course before October 4, 2011, may take an accredited refresher renovator course that includes hands-on training instead of the initial course to become certified renovators.
points.quote: Individuals who have successfully completed an accredited abatement worker or supervisor course, or individuals who successfully completed an EPA, HUD, or EPA/HUD model renovation training course before October 4, 2011 may take an accredited refresher renovator training course that includes hands-on training in lieu of the initial renovator training course to become a certified renovator.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: People who completed an accredited lead-based paint inspector or risk assessor course before October 4, 2011 may take an accredited refresher dust sampling technician course instead of the initial training. People currently certified as lead-based paint inspectors or risk assessors may act as certified dust sampling technicians without further training.
points.quote: Individuals who have successfully completed an accredited lead-based paint inspector or risk assessor course before October 4, 2011 may take an accredited refresher dust sampling technician course in lieu of the initial training to become a certified dust sampling technician. Individuals who are currently certified as lead-based paint inspectors or risk assessors may act as certified dust sampling technicians without further training.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: To keep renovator or dust sampling technician certification, an individual must complete an accredited refresher course (EPA-accredited under 745.225 or accredited by an authorized State or Tribal program) within 5 years of the date they completed the initial course.
points.quote: To maintain renovator certification or dust sampling technician certification, an individual must complete a renovator or dust sampling technician refresher course accredited by EPA under § 745.225 or by a State or Tribal program that is authorized under Subpart Q of this part within 5 years of the date the individual completed the initial course described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: An individual who does not complete a refresher course within that time must re-take the initial course to become certified again.
points.quote: If the individual does not complete a refresher course within this time, the individual must re-take the initial course to become certified again.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A renovator refresher course without hands-on training certifies the individual for 3 years from the training date; a refresher course with hands-on training certifies for 5 years. After a refresher without hands-on training, the next refresher must include hands-on training to keep renovator certification.
points.quote: Individuals who take a renovator refresher course that does not include hands-on training will be certified for 3 years from the date they complete the training. Individuals who take a refresher training course that includes hands-on training will be certified for 5 years. Individuals who take the renovator refresher without hands-on training must, for their next refresher course, take a refresher course that includes hands-on training to maintain renovator certification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Renovator and dust sampling technician responsibilities

points.text: Certified renovators are responsible for ensuring compliance with the work practice standards in 745.85 at every renovation they are assigned to.
points.quote: Certified renovators are responsible for ensuring compliance with § 745.85 at all renovations to which they are assigned.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: A certified renovator must perform all of the tasks in 745.85(b) and must either perform or direct workers who perform all of the tasks in 745.85(a) (one of the options).
points.quote: Must perform all of the tasks described in § 745.85(b) and must either perform or direct workers who perform all of the tasks described in § 745.85(a).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: On-the-job worker training: the certified renovator must train workers on the 745.85(a) work practices they will be using in performing their assigned tasks.
points.quote: Must provide training to workers on the work practices required by § 745.85(a) that they will be using in performing their assigned tasks.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The certified renovator must be physically present at the work site when the signs are posted, while work area containment is being established, and while work area cleaning is performed.
points.quote: Must be physically present at the work site when the signs required by § 745.85(a)(1) are posted, while the work area containment required by § 745.85(a)(2) is being established, and while the work area cleaning required by § 745.85(a)(5) is performed.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The certified renovator must regularly direct other individuals' work to ensure the 745.85(a) work practices are followed, including keeping containment barriers intact and ensuring dust or debris does not spread beyond the work area.
points.quote: Must regularly direct work being performed by other individuals to ensure that the work practices required by § 745.85(a) are being followed, including maintaining the integrity of the containment barriers and ensuring that dust or debris does not spread beyond the work area.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The certified renovator must be available, either on-site or by telephone, at all times that renovations are being conducted.
points.quote: Must be available, either on-site or by telephone, at all times that renovations are being conducted.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: When the party contracting for renovation services requests it, the certified renovator must use an acceptable test kit to determine whether components to be affected contain lead-based paint.
points.quote: When requested by the party contracting for renovation services, must use an acceptable test kit to determine whether components to be affected by the renovation contain lead-based paint.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The certified renovator must have copies of their initial course completion certificate and their most recent refresher course completion certificate at the work site.
points.quote: Must have with them at the work site copies of their initial course completion certificate and their most recent refresher course completion certificate.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The certified renovator must prepare the records required by 745.86(b)(1)(ii) and (6).
points.quote: Must prepare the records required by § 745.86(b)(1)(ii) and (6).

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: When performing optional dust clearance sampling under 745.85(c), a certified dust sampling technician must collect dust samples in accordance with 745.227(e)(8), send them to a laboratory recognized by EPA under TSCA section 405(b), and compare the results to the action levels in accordance with 745.227(e)(8). The technician must also carry copies of their initial and most recent refresher course completion certificates at the work site.
points.quote: When performing optional dust clearance sampling under § 745.85(c), a certified dust sampling technician: (1) Must collect dust samples in accordance with § 745.227(e)(8), must send the collected samples to a laboratory recognized by EPA under TSCA section 405(b), and must compare the results to the action levels in accordance with § 745.227(e)(8). (2) Must have with them at the work site copies of their initial course completion certificate and their most recent refresher course completion certificate.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.90, Renovator certification and dust sampling technician certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.name: Suspension, revocation and modification

points.text: EPA may suspend, revoke, or modify an individual's certification if the individual fails to comply with Federal lead-based paint statutes or regulations, and a certified renovator's certification if the renovator fails to ensure that all assigned renovations comply with 745.85.
points.quote: EPA may suspend, revoke, or modify an individual's certification if the individual fails to comply with Federal lead-based paint statutes or regulations. EPA may also suspend, revoke, or modify a certified renovator's certification if the renovator fails to ensure that all assigned renovations comply with § 745.85.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Besides an administrative or judicial finding of violation, signing a consent agreement to settle an enforcement action counts as evidence of a failure to comply.
points.quote: In addition to an administrative or judicial finding of violation, execution of a consent agreement in settlement of an enforcement action constitutes, for purposes of this section, evidence of a failure to comply with relevant statutes or regulations.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: EPA may suspend, revoke, or modify a firm's certification if the firm submits false or misleading information to EPA in its application for certification or recertification.
points.quote: EPA may suspend, revoke, or modify a firm's certification if the firm: (i) Submits false or misleading information to EPA in its application for certification or recertification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Other grounds for action on a firm's certification: the firm fails to maintain or falsifies records required in 745.86, or the firm (or an individual performing a renovation on its behalf) fails to comply with Federal lead-based paint statutes or regulations.
points.quote: (ii) Fails to maintain or falsifies records required in § 745.86. (iii) Fails to comply, or an individual performing a renovation on behalf of the firm fails to comply, with Federal lead-based paint statutes or regulations.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Before suspending, revoking, or modifying a certification, EPA notifies the affected individual or firm in writing of, among other things, the legal and factual basis for the proposed action.
points.quote: Prior to taking action to suspend, revoke, or modify an individual's or firm's certification, EPA will notify the affected entity in writing of the following: (i) The legal and factual basis for the proposed suspension, revocation, or modification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If a hearing is requested, the Presiding Officer conducts a fair, orderly, and impartial hearing within 90 days of the request for a hearing.
points.quote: (3) The Presiding Officer will: (i) Conduct a fair, orderly, and impartial hearing within 90 days of the request for a hearing.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: If EPA determines that the public health, interest, or welfare warrants immediate action to suspend a certification before the opportunity for a hearing, it notifies the affected individual or firm, explaining why the suspension before a hearing is necessary, and notifies them of their right to request a hearing on the immediate suspension within 15 days of the suspension taking place.
points.quote: If EPA determines that the public health, interest, or welfare warrants immediate action to suspend the certification of any individual or firm prior to the opportunity for a hearing, it will: (i) Notify the affected entity in accordance with paragraph (b)(1)(i) through (b)(1)(iii) of this section, explaining why it is necessary to suspend the entity's certification before an opportunity for a hearing. (ii) Notify the affected entity of its right to request a hearing on the immediate suspension within 15 days of the suspension taking place and the procedures for the conduct of such a hearing.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Unless the decision and order specify otherwise: a suspended individual takes a refresher course to make the certification current; a revoked individual takes an initial course to become certified again; a revoked firm reapplies after the revocation ends; and a firm whose suspension ends less than 5 years after it was initially certified or re-certified does not need to do anything to re-activate its certification.
points.quote: (7) Unless the decision and order issued under paragraph (b)(3)(iii) of this section specify otherwise: (i) An individual whose certification has been suspended must take a refresher training course (renovator or dust sampling technician) in order to make his or her certification current. (ii) An individual whose certification has been revoked must take an initial renovator or dust sampling technician course in order to become certified again. (iii) A firm whose certification has been revoked must reapply for certification after the revocation ends in order to become certified again. If the firm's certification has been suspended and the suspension ends less than 5 years after the firm was initially certified or re-certified, the firm does not need to do anything to re-activate its certification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.91, Suspending, revoking, or modifying an individual's or firm's certification (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.notCovered: The full notice contents in 745.91(b)(1)(ii)–(iv), the other hearing steps in (b)(2)–(3), public availability of records in (b)(5) and EPA's public list in (b)(6) are not covered point by point.

topics.name: Fees (without amounts)

points.text: No fee is imposed on training programs operated by a State, federally recognized Indian Tribe, local government, or non-profit organization. This exemption does not apply to the certification of firms or individuals.
points.quote: No fee shall be imposed on any training program operated by a State, federally recognized Indian Tribe, local government, or non-profit organization. This exemption does not apply to the certification of firms or individuals.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.92, Fees for the accreditation of renovation and dust sampling technician training and the certification of renovation firms (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: No fee is charged for accreditation or certification amendments.
points.quote: No fee will be charged for accreditation or certification amendments.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.92, Fees for the accreditation of renovation and dust sampling technician training and the certification of renovation firms (as of Nov 4, 2026)

topics.notCovered: Fee amounts (745.92(b)) and the certificate replacement fee (745.92(b)(2) and (c)) are intentionally not stated here; check the current regulation text.

topics.name: Renovator and dust sampling technician courses

points.text: A training program may seek accreditation for courses in inspector, risk assessor, supervisor, project designer, abatement worker, renovator, and dust sampling technician disciplines, and for refresher courses in each.
points.quote: A training program may seek accreditation to offer courses in any of the following disciplines: Inspector, risk assessor, supervisor, project designer, abatement worker, renovator, and dust sampling technician. A training program may also seek accreditation to offer refresher courses for each of the above listed disciplines.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.225, Accreditation of training programs: target housing and child occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The training manager designates a qualified principal instructor for each course. The instructor must have experience, education, or training in teaching workers or adults; must have completed at least 16 hours of EPA-accredited or EPA-authorized State or Tribal-accredited lead-specific instructor training for instructors of lead-based paint activities courses, or 8 hours of such training for instructors of renovator or dust sampling technician courses; and must have experience, education, or training in lead or asbestos abatement, painting, carpentry, renovation, remodeling, occupational safety and health, or industrial hygiene.
points.quote: The training manager shall designate a qualified principal instructor for each course who has: (i) Demonstrated experience, education, or training in teaching workers or adults; and (ii) Successfully completed at least 16 hours of any EPA-accredited or EPA-authorized State or Tribal-accredited lead-specific training for instructors of lead-based paint activities courses or 8 hours of any EPA-accredited or EPA-authorized State or Tribal-accredited lead-specific training for instructors of renovator or dust sampling technician courses; and (iii) Demonstrated experience, education, or training in lead or asbestos abatement, painting, carpentry, renovation, remodeling, occupational safety and health, or industrial hygiene.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.225, Accreditation of training programs: target housing and child occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: The renovator course and the dust sampling technician course must each last a minimum of 8 training hours, with a minimum of 2 hours of hands-on training activities.
points.quote: (vi) The renovator course must last a minimum of 8 training hours, with a minimum of 2 hours devoted to hands-on training activities. The minimum curriculum requirements for the renovator course are contained in paragraph (d)(6) of this section. (vii) The dust sampling technician course must last a minimum of 8 training hours, with a minimum of 2 hours devoted to hands-on training activities.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.225, Accreditation of training programs: target housing and child occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Electronic learning and other alternative delivery methods are permitted for the classroom portion of renovator, dust sampling technician, or lead-based paint activities courses, but not for the hands-on portion or for final course tests or proficiency tests.
points.quote: Electronic learning and other alternative course delivery methods are permitted for the classroom portion of renovator, dust sampling technician, or lead-based paint activities courses but not the hands-on portion of these courses, or for final course tests or proficiency tests described in paragraph (c)(7) of this section.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.225, Accreditation of training programs: target housing and child occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: For each course the training program conducts either a course test at the end (and, if applicable, a hands-on skills assessment) or a proficiency test (one of the options). To pass, a student must complete the hands-on skills assessment and pass the course test, or complete a proficiency test.
points.quote: For each course offered, the training program shall conduct either a course test at the completion of the course, and if applicable, a hands-on skills assessment, or in the alternative, a proficiency test for that discipline. Each student must successfully complete the hands-on skills assessment and receive a passing score on the course test to pass any course, or successfully complete a proficiency test.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.225, Accreditation of training programs: target housing and child occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Renovator and dust sampling technician course completion certificates include an accurate, recognizable photograph of the individual, not smaller than 1 square inch as reproduced. Renovator certificates also show the expiration date of certification.
points.quote: (vii) For renovator and dust sampling technician course completion certificates, a photograph of the individual. The photograph must be an accurate and recognizable image of the individual. As reproduced on the certificate, the photograph must not be smaller than 1 square inch. (viii) For renovator course completion certificates, the expiration date of certification.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.225, Accreditation of training programs: target housing and child occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

points.text: Renovator course topics include renovation methods to minimize the creation of dust and lead-based paint hazards, interior and exterior containment and cleanup methods, and methods to ensure the renovation has been properly completed, including cleaning verification and clearance testing.
points.quote: (vi) Renovation methods to minimize the creation of dust and lead-based paint hazards. (vii) Interior and exterior containment and cleanup methods. (viii) Methods to ensure that the renovation has been properly completed, including cleaning verification and clearance testing.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.225, Accreditation of training programs: target housing and child occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)
